projects.title: Playwright UI framework
projects.description: End-to-end tests for a demo online shop (automationexercise.com): sign-up, login, products, cart and checkout, plus its public API. Every test brings its own throwaway user, so they all run in parallel.

details.v: The site under test is a shared public demo: slow, full of ads, and it answers "queue full" under load. Tests that share accounts or wait on ads turn flaky fast.
Page objects for the UI. Fixtures create a fresh user through the site's API before each test and delete it after, so no test depends on another. Ad requests are blocked at the network level.
12 UI flows (auth, products, cart, checkout) on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, plus 5 API specs in a browserless project. Specs only ask for the fixtures they need; assertions stay in the specs.

GitHub Actions in the official Playwright container: a quality gate first (Prettier, ESLint, tsc), then one job per suite. @smoke on pull requests, @regression on every push and every night, at most 2 suites at once so the site keeps up.

Running in CI, with an Allure dashboard on GitHub Pages: history, trends, flaky tests, and a screenshot and video for every failure. Next on the roadmap: a Dockerfile, more flows, a Playwright upgrade.

tiles.original: Contributed to a large-scale REST API to GraphQL migration by identifying and documenting migration gaps, analyzing schemas and API contracts, resolving integration and functionality issues, and supporting builds, deployments, configuration changes, and end-to-end validation.

tiles.title: Fixed environments that blocked testing

tiles.title: Put the tests into the release pipeline

tiles.title: Wrote down what was learned
